html:
Northern Rhodesia was a British protectorate in south central Africa from 1911 to 1964, now the independent country of Zambia. The map shows it in 1938 and 1945.

The British South Africa Company ruled it at first, partly through treaties with the Lozi kingdom of Barotseland. The British government took over in 1924. Soon after, huge copper deposits were opened up along the Copperbelt near the Congo border, and by the late 1930s the territory was one of the world's major copper producers. African miners struck in 1935 and 1940 over pay and taxes. The capital moved to the new city of Lusaka in 1935.

Against African opposition, Britain joined the territory with Southern Rhodesia and Nyasaland in the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland in 1953. Nationalists led by Kenneth Kaunda fought it, and in 1964 the country became independent as Zambia.
sum: Northern Rhodesia was a British protectorate in south central Africa from 1911 to 1964, now the independent country of Zambia. The map shows it in 1938 and 1945.
